chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn Isma'il from a man from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a man who forgets one prostration from his prayer. He said: 'If he remembers it before bowing, he performs it and builds upon his prayer, then performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness after concluding. And if he remembers it after bowing, he repeats the prayer. And forgetting the prostration in the first two [rak'ahs] and the last two [is] the same.'

Therefore, this report is not contradictory to the first report, because his saying (peace be upon him): 'and forgetting the prostration in the first two and the last two is the same,' he meant by it the leaving of both prostrations together. Do you not see that what the report contained only contained the ruling of one who left both prostrations together, because he said: 'If he remembers it after bowing, he repeats the prayer.' So, if the meaning of remembering the prostration were not [remembering] the two together, it would not be obligatory to repeat the prayer, according to what we have established. And that which he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person forgets a prostration during prayer and remembers it after bowing?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the precise jurisprudential distinction between forgetting a single prostration versus both, determining whether the prayer requires simple correction with 'sajdat al-ghaflah' or full repetition (i'adah). The accompanying commentary clarifies that the condition for repeating the prayer applies specifically when the omission of both prostrations is realized after the first bowing (ruku'), ensuring consistency with other hadiths. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining the structural integrity of prayer components while providing practical leniency for minor omissions.
